Interactive dashboards for ATP and WTA players: surface splits, form trends, and full head-to-head records, updated after every match.

Serve, return, and rally patterns mapped as colour-coded heatmaps and radar charts that read at a glance, not as rows of numbers.

Pressure Points

Our own metric, built in-house: how players hold up in the tightest moments of a match, scored point by point. Not break points - something no other site tracks.

From the editors

TennisRatio has covered the ATP and WTA tours daily since 2022, from Grand Slams to the Challenger and ITF circuits. What sets our reporting apart is the layer underneath it: a suite of original metrics we've built in-house, including pressure points, dominance ratios, and match efficiency scores. These feed into interactive player dashboards with charts and visualisations that drill into surface splits, pressure situations, and form trends. We've held press accreditation at events such as Stuttgart, Madrid, Abu Dhabi and Ostrava, most recently the WTA 500 Berlin Tennis Open.

Editorial team

Maciej Myrta

Founder & Editor-in-Chief

I built TennisRatio as a place where tennis writing and data live side by side: where numbers become charts you can actually read and stories get backed by underlying stats. I specialize in WTA coverage as it's the tour I know best, and before this I spent years producing sports content for fan communities online.

Paweł Roztocki

Editor & Writer

Covering both tours week to week, writing our daily reports with a focus on what the data says about the next match, not just what happened in the last one. I will take a first round at a 250 in South America over most second-week Grand Slam matches, and defend that call with the draw sheet in hand.

Cataldo Ferrara

Writer & Correspondent

I cover ATP previews and recaps at TennisRatio. I start from the numbers, but I'm drawn to the mental battles behind them, especially the players whose mental game stands out under pressure. I've been on court my whole life, though unfortunately my analytical side is still sharper than my backhand.
